newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Costa Rica envoy quits after row.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Costa Rica envoy quits after row.

text.p: Mexico's ambassador to Costa Rica quit on Monday after his comments that the Central American nation was ruled by an "oligarchy" caused an uproar.

In a resignation letter issued by the Foreign Ministry, the ambassador, Jose Rafael Castelazo, said his decision was taken "because of the firm conviction that by remaining in the post I would no longer contribute to the strengthening of ties between Mexico and that sister nation (Costa Rica)."
Castelazo caused a stir in Costa Rica with a series of critical comments published in the Mexican weekly magazine Siempre about the Costa Rican political and economic system.
"Even though there are two strong parties (in Costa Rica), it's the same oligarchy," Castelazo said referring to the ruling National Liberation Party and the opposition Social Christian Unit.
He also said the government of President Jose Maria Figueres "is practically paralysed because it can't make a decision."
Costa Rica demanded a retraction, but Castelazo offered neither a retraction nor an apology. In his letter, he simply described the country as "very dearly loved...to all Mexicans".
Earlier, Costa Rican Foreign Minister Fernando Naranjo told Reuters that the situation had been resolved after he and his Mexican counterpart Jose Angel Gurria talked by telephone over the weekend.
"This unfortunate incident is now history, and of course it will not affect the very good relations between the two countries," Naranjo said in a telephone interview.
The remarks by Castelazo, who had just taken the post on May 22, angered Costa Ricans, who see their Central American country as relatively advanced and sophisticated.
